questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: a university with big facilities and a lot of reseach in the equine hospital department

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A lot of information at copenhagen university website about the master and under "plan your master". The website was not fully updated about what courses there was available in utrecht, so I had to contact the "Coordinator International Office and Admissions" and she helped a lot!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved information about my scheduel on my email. I also got help to find the right building, what to remember and so on from the international coordinator.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There is a lot on facebook, which is ok if you are fast. but it's also expensive...

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: its very nice to live in utrecht city center or close by. you can easily get around with a bike otherwise there is also metro and busses going to the campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The host institution refers to short stay housing which is not possible when you are "only" staying for 10-12 weeks, which doesn't really make sense. If we are not short stay then who is?.... A little too bad, beacuse it would be very nice to get help to find housing from the host university.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: mail correspondence with the international coordinator

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: mail, but very easy

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I chose one class, and I got into that one. very succesfull.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: send an email to the international coordinator to register and get information.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of my course was very good and I learned a lot

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more practical teaching and teaching in the stables at the equine hospital. Every week the students could also choose a subject we wanted to discuss, where we sat down 1-1,5 hour to discuss.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Equine clinic

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Equine clinic - a lot of hands on and practical skills. Also a big caseload and a lot of patients to discuss

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: i don't really know because I didn't looked up the opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: i dont know

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I went to yoga a couple of places in the city center. There is also plenty of other sports and training/fitness opportunities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Be a tourist in the netherlands! Lots of places to see. Utecht city center is also very nice and cosy and you can go for a walk around, go up in the dom tower, explore dom under, go canoing/cayaking, try the coffeeshops, go to restaurant adn cafees, go for a bike to the the castle outside utrecht and so on...

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy, they are very sweet and easy to talk with

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: not really..

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The dutch students and teachers were very openminded and easy to talk to.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Enjoy your stay
2. Take the oppertunity to be at the hospital as much as possible - that way you will learn more
3. Be openminded and take notes

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: its nice to have some of the books with you and you notes, so you can go home and look things up.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Everything I learned, seen, experienced and all the people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: hmm maybe the language in the beginning - both me and the other students just had to switch to english and sometimes there was some academic words we didn't know.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
